provenance.note: SLOT 21, AND THE BINARY SAYS SO RATHER THAN THE WIKI: routine 0 is `lea $1fa(pc),a3 / move.l a3,$238(a5) / moveq #$14,d0`, and ($238-$f8)/16+1 is 21 on the ExtAdr layout (+Equ.s:1185) with $14 the slot zero-based. SymBase's Installer claims 21 too and its routine 0 makes the same store, which is not a conflict: they are one product at two ages and only one of them is ever loaded.

notes: REPLACES AN AMOSTOOLS STUB. Until 2026-08-12 this row held only the token table with the library stripped out from under it -- both length fields zero, no code, every routine word overwritten with `====` -- so the tier could not rise above `manual`. The real library's table is IDENTICAL to the stub's, entry for entry, id for id and spec for spec, which is a check on the AMOSTools reader as much as on this registration. What changes is that the code is now here to read. DBENCH AND SYMBASE ARE THE SAME PRODUCT AT TWO AGES, both by Lázár Zoltán. dbench-0.42's 23 named keywords are symbase-0.94's first 23 in the same order, and all but the last two at the same ids -- `db sel`, `db use`, `db address`, `db close`, `db flen`, `db fieldno`, `db saved on`, `db saved off` and on. Neither should be ported without the other open. SymBase 0.92's readme records a keyword REMOVAL -- "REM: Date functions removed to a separate extension / No more needs date.library" -- which is exactly the shape that makes one build's tokens detokenise to nonsense under another, so the `renumbered` verdict may apply across the family and has not been checked. THE ARCHIVE'S BEST EVIDENCE IS NOT THE GUIDE: `Symbiose.AMOS`, 29,912 bytes, is a complete application written against this extension, and a program that uses a keyword settles what it does better than a paragraph describing it. `Tools/CreateDBF` is a companion, `OBUDAAT.DBF` a 62KB sample database in dBASE III format -- so the on-disc format is a documented one and the port would not have to guess it -- and four .abk banks carry the interface graphics. THE TWO TABLES ARE NOT ID-COMPATIBLE, and this is the `renumbered` case the sweep exists to catch. DBench's 23 named entries are SymBase's first 22 at identical ids and then diverge: id $0166 is DBench's `db goto` and SymBase's `db get`, and $0174 is DBench's `db put` and SymBase's `db getf`. 0.94 inserted `Db Get` and `Db Getf` there and pushed `Db Goto` out to $0182 and `Db Put$` to $0190. So a DBench program's `Db Goto n` read against SymBase's table detokenises as `Db Get`, which is a FUNCTION with spec `00` where `db goto` is an instruction with `I0` -- it does not merely do the wrong thing, it will not parse. Binding the right identity is what keeps the two apart, and dispatch is by NAME, so one port serves both. BOTH CLAIM SLOT 21 AND THE BINARIES SAY SO: DBench routine 0 is `move.l a3,$238(a5) / moveq #$14,d0` and SymBase's is the same store, and ($238-$f8)/16+1 is 21 on the ExtAdr layout (+Equ.s:1185). They cannot be loaded together, which is what successive builds of one product are supposed to do.
